title: Marketplace FinTech Onboarding Checklist and Risk Snippets
body:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact checklist and copy/snippet bank tailored for listing Redwood Inference in cloud marketplaces for FinTech verticals (banking, payments, lending, capital markets). It bundles the technical and legal acceptance gates we commonly miss during marketplace onboarding, plus short sales/landing tile copy and risk mitigations to accelerate approval and pilot conversions.

Notes on audience and usage:
- Primary: Marketplace ops + Partner PMs preparing a verticalized tile and acceptance package.
- Secondary: Sales enablement, Solutions Eng, Legal for quick review.
- Status: Draft — intended to be a lean checklist to attach to marketplace intake.

Summary checklist (high level) — green box preflight
1) Product fit and tile assets
   - Tile title: short, explicit (<= 60 chars). Example: "Redwood Inference — Low-latency LLM Inference for Regulated FinTech"
   - Short description (<= 250 chars) and 1-line value props (3 bullets).
   - Hero image + screenshots demonstrating console metrics (latency, per-route cost).
   - 1-minute demo video (hosted, captioned) showing quickstart and private deployment snippet.

2) Compliance & data residency
   - Confirm data residency options supported: list regions and VPC/private deploy availability.
   - KYC/data handling statement for customers: outline what we log, retention, and optional customer-managed KMS support.
   - Provide SOC2 status and link to report; include contact for security questionnaire.
   - If listing in EU/UK fintech marketplaces, include DPA template and data-processing descriptions.

3) Technical acceptance (must-haves)
   - Trial plan / sandbox flow: specify credentials, trial quotas, expiration, and sample payloads. Provide a runnable cURL + SDK quickstart targeted at the FinTech use-case (redaction example: ACH routing, PII masking).
   - Verified endpoints for private/dedicated deployments and routing fallback policies (important for SLA gating).
   - Billing SKU mapping and entitlement matrix: trial SKU, paid SKU, reserved capacity SKU. Attach sample billing call flow for marketplace metering.
   - E2E smoke tests that marketplace QA can run (script link). Include expected response time SLA thresholds for small/medium/large workloads.

4) Security & integration details
   - Allowed network ingress/egress patterns for private deployments (IP ranges, peering guide).
   - KMS/HSM integration instructions for customer-managed keys.
   - Notes on secrets rotation and how marketplace provisioned credentials map to Redwood API keys.

5) Legal and commercial gates
   - Standard enterprise terms + any marketplace-specific amendments.
   - Refunds and trial termination policy for sandbox accounts.
   - Liability caps and data breach notification timelines customized for regulated customers.

6) Marketing and go-to-market copy requirements
   - 1-line elevator for tile (<= 120 chars).
   - 3 short bullets that surface measurable outcomes (latency, cost reduction, compliance support).
   - Suggested CTA flows (Start free trial, Contact sales for dedicated, Request private deployment).

7) Observability & onboarding support artifacts
   - Link to quickstart playbook and architecture diagram for marketplace listing.
   - Prebuilt demo dataset and prompts safe for FinTech (synthetic data set).
   - Contact for 24–72hr technical support for marketplace QA plus escalation path.

Risk snippets and mitigations (to paste into acceptance notes)
- Risk: Marketplace reviewers flag data residency mismatch.
  Mitigation: Attach region-by-region deployment options table and describe customer choice to pin region and KMS.

- Risk: Reviewer asks for PII handling proof for financial data.
  Mitigation: Provide redaction examples, our SDK helper that masks common identifiers, and the synthetic demo corpus used in sandbox.

- Risk: QA sees latency outliers on larger sequences.
  Mitigation: Attach recommended prompt truncation guidance, batching configs, and model profile recommending quantized variants for throughput.

- Risk: Billing SKU mapping ambiguous for reserved capacity.
  Mitigation: Provide explicit SKU matrix (trial vs pay-as-you-go vs reserved) and example invoice lines.

Tile copy bank (short, editable snippets)
- Tile headline options (pick one):
  • "Low-latency LLM inference for regulated FinTech teams"
  • "Ship secure, predictable LLM features — private or hosted"
  • "Inference tuned for latency, cost, and compliance"

- Short description (one-liner):
  • "Redwood Inference delivers predictable, production-grade LLM serving with private deployment options, per-route observability, and cost controls for financial applications."

- 3 bullet benefits (marketplace tile):
  • "Sub-100ms tail latencies in hosted mode; dedicated pools for predictable throughput."
  • "Customer-managed keys and VPC options for regulatory compliance."
  • "Plug-in SDKs, sandbox trials, and rollout controls to prevent regression."

- 30–50 word sales elevator for FinTech PMs:
  • "If your team needs LLM features that meet regulatory constraints and predictable economics, Redwood Inference provides a single runtime for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — with per-route observability, KMS integrations, and an upgrade path from sandbox to reserved capacity."

Approval checklist for marketplace intake packet (attach before submission)
- [ ] Final tile copy (headline + 250-char description)
- [ ] Hero image and 2 screenshots (console + demo)
- [ ] Short demo video link
- [ ] Trial provisioning instructions + sample credentials
- [ ] SOC2 / security pack link and contact
- [ ] DPA template for EU/UK listings
- [ ] Billing SKU mapping doc and sample invoice line
- [ ] E2E smoke test script and expected SLA numbers
- [ ] Escalation contact for QA (email + slack)
